README: Java classes the coverage threshold does not apply to, each with the reason and a test
that makes the reason expire.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
The coverage standard this repository holds itself to names Python and TypeScript, each
gated independently at 90% and never blended. This plugin is a third language, and the
standard did not mention it. That is not permission to ship ungated, so
assert-coverage.py applies the same 90% to this tree and reports it as its own number.
The header comment of .github/workflows/ash-typescript-ci.yml explains at length why a
bare percentage is not enough: a threshold can be satisfied by measuring less, and the
shrink looks like a config tidy-up in review. That workflow pairs its threshold with
assert-coverage-scope.mjs, which pins the file count and the statement denominator, and
assert-coverage-completeness.mjs, which requires a reason for every exclusion.
The same reasoning applies here, and the mechanism differs because the tool differs.
jest omits source that no test imports from the report ENTIRELY, so an unmeasured file
is invisible. JaCoCo enumerates compiled classes, so a class no test touches appears at
0% -- it is visibly bad rather than absent. The gameable move here is therefore not a
narrowed crawler root but a widened exclusion pattern: one line in this file, and the
percentage rises without a test being written. So this file is the thing the gate audits
hardest, and assert-coverage.py is the only place the 90% is enforced -- Gradle's own
jacocoTestCoverageVerification is deliberately not used, because two enforcers of one
number means two places to relax it.
KINDS, AND WHAT MAKES AN ENTRY STALE
The kind is not a label; it selects which staleness test runs, so an entry that stops
being true fails the gate instead of being carried forward.
ide-glue -- the class exists only to satisfy an IntelliJ Platform extension point.
Measuring it means starting an IDE, which this build deliberately does not do.
Every such entry carries maxLines, and the gate re-measures the file: the budget is
what stops the exclusion becoming a place to hide logic. All three entries below are
written so that each decision they could have made lives in a measured class instead,
and the budget is the mechanical check on that claim. Stale once the file stops being
tracked, once it exceeds its budget, or once it turns up covered in the report.
WHAT DOES NOT BELONG HERE
A class a plain JUnit test could measure but no test exercises. That is a coverage gap
and belongs in a test. Excluding it would restore exactly the blind spot the gate exists
to remove.
Paths are repository-relative and POSIX-separated. classPattern is matched against the
JaCoCo report's fully-qualified class name, including any nested class, so a nested class
inside an excluded file is excluded with it.

exclusions.reason: Implements com.intellij.lang.annotation.ExternalAnnotator. Its three overrides need a PsiFile, an Editor and an AnnotationHolder, none of which can be constructed outside a running IDE, so measuring it means either starting a headless IDE per test run or asserting on mocks of the platform's own classes. Every decision it could make has been moved out: which findings belong to this file and where they land is AshAnnotationPlanner, whether a scan may run and what failed is AshScanService and AshVersionProbe, where output goes is AshOutputDirectory. What remains is field reads, a null guard, a relativize, and a switch from AshSeverity to HighlightSeverity. The 140-line budget is the check on that sentence.

A PersistentStateComponent. Instantiating it outside an IDE is possible; exercising it is not, because getInstance() goes through ApplicationManager and loadState() through the platform's XmlSerializerUtil, and a test that called neither would be asserting that two public fields hold what was written to them. Everything that could be wrong about the executablePath value is decided in AshExecutable.resolve, which is measured -- including that empty means the default rather than being stored as a literal.

A Swing settings page built with the platform's FormBuilder and JB* components. createComponent() constructs widgets and the other four methods copy values between those widgets and AshSettings, so a test would be asserting that a JBTextField returns the text it was given. The one thing in it that carries meaning rather than wiring is the hint text naming automated-security-helper for the ash name collision, and AshVersionProbeTest asserts that same recommendation reaches the user through the error path, which is where they will actually meet it.
